explanation: The pole fires at the word that introduces a span or point of time - the determiner or preposition just before it (' the', ' this', ' my', ' his', ' on'), or its first subword when there is none ('zaterdag', 'OCTOBER', 'Nisan', '250th', '今年') - whenever the context so far makes what follows a period of time rather than a thing: 'the entire afternoon', 'the whole night', 'the following week', 'the previous December', 'this morning', 'his 14th birthday', a date, day, month, holiday, or a date-format field in calendar code. It stays at its floor where the same determiner introduces an object, even with the same adjective and the same token count ('The rain continued the entire afternoon' 11.5 vs 'The rain flooded the entire valley' 0.9; 'The storm raged the entire night' 6.9 vs 'The storm flooded the entire old street' 0.1), so what decides it is the verb or preposition before the determiner, not the determiner, the adjective or the word after it.
